reasons: The rule is genuinely unmet: §2(d) reserves only TrueLink's rights in the Interface, and nothing in the cited text gives Client ownership of Support Services work product or the fallback's perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense results — so the clause fails the fallback on a material term and 'deviation' is the correct classification rather than over-flagging an acceptable fallback.

The rationale correctly distinguishes the §10 confidentiality treatment of Client's IP and Support Services results (a secrecy obligation, not ownership) and the §13 reservation limited to discontinuation of Hosting Services, and correctly declines to treat the §8(d) non-exclusive Credit Data licence as a walk-away assignment or to double-flag it.

The redline is actionable and tracks the redline guidance with a minimal additive fix: a new §2(e) reserving Client Content/IP/data ownership, assigning Support Services work product to Client, granting a licence-back for embedded TrueLink IP, and barring joint ownership; it leaves the counterparty-favourable §2(d) Interface ownership intact and does not disturb the existing §8(d) licence (retained title is compatible with a non-exclusive licence).

The comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, explains what changed and why, cites the playbook position and offers the fallback; the deterministic checks (operation applies, no residual assignment of Customer IP/Data to Vendor) are consistent with the substance of the edit.
